o: the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha and the first session of each year

new.x: Article 87 requires a special address at the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha and at the first session of each year. new.tq: Art. 86 = may address any time; Art. 87 = must address: first session after election + first session of each year.

new.s:
With reference to a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249, consider the following statements:
1. It must be supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. It remains in force for one year and may be extended one year at a time.
3. It authorises the State Legislatures to make laws on a Union List subject.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct: the resolution needs two-thirds of members present and voting. Statement 2 is correct: it is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 249 lets Parliament legislate on a State List subject in the national interest; it does not authorise State Legislatures. Hence 1 and 2 only.
new.tq: Art. 249: RS (2/3 present and voting) lets PARLIAMENT enter the State List for 1 year at a time.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. While a resolution for his removal is under consideration, he cannot preside but may speak, and he cannot vote.
3. When the Vice-President acts as President, the Deputy Chairman performs the duties of the Chairman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Vice-President is ex officio Chairman (Arts. 64 and 89). Statement 2 is correct: unlike the Speaker, who can vote in the first instance during his removal proceedings, the Chairman cannot vote at all while his removal is pending, though he may speak. Statement 3 is correct: under Article 91 the Deputy Chairman presides when the Chairman's office is vacant or the Vice-President is acting as President. Hence all three.
new.tq: Speaker under removal: can vote (first instance). Chairman under removal: cannot vote at all.

new.tq: First Chairman: S. Radhakrishnan; present Chairman: C.P. Radhakrishnan.

new.x: A privilege motion is governed by Rule 222 of the Lok Sabha rules and Rule 187 of the Rajya Sabha rules. Rule 184 (LS) is a discussion followed by a vote, Rule 193 (LS) is a short-duration discussion without a vote, Rule 180A-E (RS) covers Special Mentions, and Rule 198 (LS) is the no-confidence motion.

The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (the Vice-President) does not preside over a joint sitting, the President only summons it, and there is no rule for the senior-most Lok Sabha member.
new.tq: Joint sitting chair: Speaker > Deputy Speaker > RS Deputy Chairman; never the VP/Chairman.

new.s:
With reference to timelines for assent to State Bills, consider the following statements:
1. In the Tamil Nadu Governor case (April 2025), the Supreme Court laid down fixed timelines for Governors and applied 'deemed assent'.
2. In November 2025, a five-judge Bench, giving its advisory opinion on a Presidential Reference, held that courts cannot fix such timelines or declare deemed assent.
3. The November 2025 opinion upheld the deemed assent granted in the Tamil Nadu case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct: the April 2025 Tamil Nadu Governor judgment introduced fixed timelines and deemed assent. Statement 2 is correct: the five-judge Bench's advisory opinion on the Presidential Reference (November 2025) held that courts cannot fix such timelines or declare deemed assent. Statement 3 is wrong: that opinion is contrary to deemed assent, not an endorsement of it. Hence 1 and 2 only.
new.tq: Apr 2025 TN case: deemed assent + timelines; Nov 2025 Presidential Reference opinion: courts cannot do either.

Consider the following statements regarding the Appropriation Bill under Article 114:
1. No amendment may be proposed that would vary the amount or alter the destination of any grant voted by the Lok Sabha.
2. An amendment may vary the amount of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
3. The Bill carries an automatic repeal clause.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct: no amendment may vary the amount or alter the destination of a voted grant. Statement 2 is wrong: charged expenditure also cannot be varied by amendment. Statement 3 is correct: the Appropriation Bill carries an automatic repeal clause. Hence 1 and 3 only.
